data.gender_notes: Gaganaapriya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who loves the sky; derived from the words 'gagana' meaning sky and 'apriya' meaning beloved. The name Gaganaapriya carries the meaning “Sky Lover” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gaganaapriya usually hope their child will grow to embody sky lover and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Living in the moment and finding joy in the beauty of the universe.
data.etymology: Gaganaapriya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sky Lover.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gaganaapriya total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

The love and appreciation for the celestial realm is reflected in this name, emphasising the inherent wonder and awe for the natural world that Hindu philosophy holds.

historical_references.reference: Gaganaapriya is a name mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata. It is the name of a celestial nymph, or Gandharvi, named Subha who is the wife of the planet Jupiter (Buddha). She is described as having a beautiful face and a gentle nature, and is the goddess of the sky.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that forms a major part of the Indian mythology. It is a vast work of 100,000 shlokas (verses) divided into 18 parvas (books). The epic describes the Kurukshetra war between the Pandava and Kaurava princes and their allies.

historical_references.reference: Gaganaapriya is also the name of a goddess worshipped in the Hindu religion, particularly in the regions of Karnataka and Maharashtra in India. She is believed to be the goddess of the sky and the protector of the universe. She is often depicted with a white complexion, multiple arms, and holding lotus flowers.
historical_references.context: Hinduism is the world's third largest religion and has a rich mythology and theology. The Hindu pantheon includes millions of gods and goddesses, each with their unique characteristics and roles. The worship of regional deities is common in Hinduism.
